text:
Maria Ruiz: Quick weekly check-in for Emberly — focusing on p95/p99 by route & model, and streaming vs non-streaming. Can people post the main deltas and any spikes?
Liam O'Connor: pulling numbers now, will paste a short summary.
AccountHealthBot: automated snapshot attached: https://internal.redwood/ah/emberly/1834507890 (dashboard) :bar_chart:
Liam O'Connor: TL;DR — overall traffic up 12% w/ streaming requests up 28%. p95 streaming is stable, p99 has a small tail on the /chat route for Model-B-quant.
Liam O'Connor: here are the p95/p99s I pulled (last 7d). copying raw table: 
```
route,model,streaming,p95_ms,p99_ms
/chat,Model-A,non-stream,140,320
/chat,Model-A,stream,120,280
/chat,Model-B-quant,non-stream,160,650
/chat,Model-B-quant,stream,150,720
/embeddings,Emb-Base,non-stream,90,220
/embeddings,Emb-Base,stream,85,210
/rerank,RankNet-v2,non-stream,110,300
/rerank,RankNet-v2,stream,105,290
```
Maria Ruiz: Noted the Model-B-quant p99 jump on streaming — 720ms is high compared to others. Is that correlated with cache misses or bursts? :eyes:
Noah Patel: I checked cache hit rates — for chat Model-B-quant streaming the prefix cache hit dropped from 86% to 57% during the largest spike window (Thu 09:10-09:40 UTC). Likely cause.
Tara Chen: any correlated infra events? I don't see node restarts in that window. Autoscaler did one small scale-up at 09:08 for the dedicated pool.
Liam O'Connor: also saw an uptick in 503s for the same model+route: error rate from 0.08% -> 0.6% during the tail. Might be graceful degradation hitting fallback path more often.
Sophie Alvarez: onboarding team note — Emberly rolled a new prompt deployment Wed night that increases token length average by ~18%. That could push sequence lengths and KV pressure.
Maria Ruiz: that fits: longer prefixes -> lower cache hit -> higher p99. Is this expected behavior for Model-B-quant?
Tara Chen: Model-B-quant is more sensitive to sequence length due to KV cache eviction frequency on the quantized kernels. We should check batching and max_batch_ms config for streaming.
Noah Patel: I'll look at the streaming KV cache eviction logs and share the delta by shard. Also will check if falling back to Model-A occurred more often (fallback rate).
Liam O'Connor: For next steps I propose: 1) increase prefix cache TTL for Emberly in dedicated pool to reduce eviction, 2) temporarily route heavy streaming chat requests to Model-A if latency SLA is at risk, 3) ask Emberly CSM to advise on prompt length changes.
Maria Ruiz: agree. Liam can you estimate impact and any cost delta for routing to Model-A?
Liam O'Connor: quick guesstimate — routing 20% of streaming chat to Model-A reduces p99 to ~350ms for affected traffic; cost delta +8% on those flows.
Sophie Alvarez: I'll flag to Emberly that our recommended change is to trim prompt system tokens in the next deploy cycle; we can offer a short workshop.
Tara Chen: I'll open an infra ticket to bump prefix_cache_ttl and monitor for 24h, assigning to @Noah Patel for validation.
Noah Patel: assigned, will run a focused compare query and post results here by EOD.
Maria Ruiz: Renewal risk note — Emberly's renewal conversation is in 6 weeks. If we can stabilise p99 under 400ms for chat streaming and keep error rate <0.2%, risk should be low. Otherwise risk increases.
Liam O'Connor: Agree. Also recommend a short enablement session on prompt-length tradeoffs and how caching works — helps them avoid regressions.
Maria Ruiz: Action items summary: 
- Tara: infra ticket to bump prefix_cache_ttl (done)
- Noah: validate cache hit + p99 after TTL bump, share EOD
- Liam: simulate routing-plan cost impact and draft rollback policy
- Sophie: coordinate enablement invite with Emberly PMs
I'll check back in next Tuesday with updated snapshot. Thanks all :raised_hands:
